items.title: Goldman Sachs, SocGen buy Rs 920 crore stake in Lenskart
items.description: Goldman Sachs and Societe Generale have jointly invested ₹920 crore to purchase a 1% stake in Lenskart Solutions, acquiring 65.21 lakh and 61.76 lakh shares priced at ₹725 each. Steadview Capital Management facilitated this by selling an equivalent number of shares, resulting in their stake decreasing from 3.31% to 2.58%. Following this, Lenskart’s stock slid approximately 4%, ending the day at ₹715.90.

items.title: Stocks in news: Adani Enterprises, Tata Steel, PhysicsWallah, Hyundai Motor India, Lenskart and Hindalco
items.description: Indian equity markets experienced a decline as benchmarks reversed early gains due to profit booking. The Nifty 50 index fell significantly, indicating investor sentiment was shifting. Several companies announced developments affecting their stock performance, including Adani Enterprises and Tata Steel. Hyundai Motor India also revealed a price increase due to rising input costs across its vehicle range. Various other companies have made strategic moves, which may impact their future performance.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Indian equities have felt the heat from last week's international sell-off, with significant fallout in both the banking and commodities sectors. Experts foresee that while global equity weaknesses may spill over into the Indian market, the repercussions will be limited. Current support levels sit at 25,000-25,100 and resistance is registered at 25,500-25,600. Foreign portfolio investors have been active, buying equities worth Rs 5,672.

items.title: Indian markets face fresh volatility test after sharp rebound: Kotak Institutional Equities
items.description: Indian equities are likely to see increased volatility as domestic rallies occur alongside global market sell-offs. Concerns about the impact of global weakness on Indian markets remain present due to negative investor sentiment. Both foreign portfolio and mutual fund inflows have been positive, although insurance company flows have declined. Corporate earnings and crude oil prices are anticipated to influence the market movements in the near term.

items.title: Stock Radar: L&T stock breaks out from multi-month descending resistance trendline; time to buy?
items.description: Larsen & Toubro Ltd (L&T) stock has witnessed a breakout from its descending resistance trendline, signaling potential growth ahead. The stock has recorded more than a 13% increase this past month, following a robust base around the 3,600 mark. It's advisable for traders to consider buying, aiming for targets between Rs 4,400 and Rs 4,450 in the near future, with a stop loss strategy advised below Rs 4,050.

items.title: NBFCs tap AI to spot defaults early, lower credit costs
items.description: Non-banking financial companies are increasingly adopting AI technologies to enhance their underwriting processes and credit monitoring. L&T Finance reported significant reductions in EMI bounce rates in various portfolios after implementing AI-powered solutions. Poonawalla Fincorp noted improvements in early delinquencies and credit costs as a result of advanced risk decisioning. Kissht also experienced a decline in delinquency rates, demonstrating the effectiveness of these AI initiatives.

items.title: HDFC Bank, Kotak, Axis need faster retail deposit growth for share re-rating: Jefferies
items.description: Retail deposit growth is not keeping pace for HDFC Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, and Axis Bank when benchmarked against rivals. As per Jefferies, a push for faster deposit growth is crucial for these banks to align with projected earnings. If this trend remains stagnant, they may resort to high-cost funding strategies, negatively impacting net interest margins. Meanwhile, ICICI Bank and SBI thrive in deposits, along with faster-growing smaller private banks.

items.title: Irdai sets up panels to standardise health insurance claim rejections, enable real-time tracking
items.description: To bolster transparency within health insurance claims, Irdai has formed two specialized groups tasked with standardizing rejection reasons. Their objectives include developing consistent reporting standards and introducing a live tracking system for policyholders. The first group's focus is on analyzing claims performance metrics, including turnaround times, while the second will advise on a pilot project for timely claim status updates, with reports expected by December 26.

items.title: Blackstone brings in former HDFC Ergo CEO Ritesh Kumar for India insurance venture
items.description: Underscoring its commitment to the Indian insurance landscape, Blackstone has designated Ritesh Kumar as a 10% shareholder in its emerging general insurance initiative. Targeting the expansive non-life insurance market that surpasses ₹3 lakh crore, the venture is set to leverage advanced technology for AI-driven processes. An initial funding of ₹150-200 crore is earmarked for kickoff, while it awaits green lighting from the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India.

items.title: Banks flag NBFC autopay risks amid rising cyberfraud cases
items.description: Rising cybersecurity issues are prompting banks to scrutinize the pre-authorisation practices of non-banking finance companies, which permit unmonitored financial transactions. In light of this, banks are urging for more stringent oversight to reinforce automated payment systems. The Reserve Bank of India is actively engaging with financial institutions and technology firms to tackle these vulnerabilities, highlighting the necessity of periodic assessments of NBFC infrastructures to uphold security against potential fraud.
